newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. envoy flies to France to discuss Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy flies to France to discuss Zaire.

text.p: U.S. envoy Bill Richardson left Cape Town for Paris on Wednesday to consult France on the crisis in Zaire, where rebels are advancing on the capital Kinshasa and President Mobutu Sese Seko prepared for a trip out of the country.

Richardson, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, left South Africa aboard a U.S. air force plane and was due to put down for one refuelling stop on the 6,000-mile (10,000 km) flight to France. It was not clear where the aircraft would touch down.

The envoy has been shuttling between the Zaire factions and neighbouring countries trying to avert a bloody end to the Zaire conflict. He was in South Africa on Tuesday for talks with Vice President Thabo Mbeki.

The Zairean rebel forces of Laurent Kabila say they are less than 50 miles (85 km) from Kinshasa and have appealed for government troops to surrender to avoid a bloody takeover of the capital. Diplomatic sources say the front line is more like 125 miles (200 km) from Kinshasa.

President Mobutu was due to travel to Libreville in nearby Gabon on Wednesday for an African mini summit and while a spokesman said he would return to his capital two days later, rumours swirled that this was a fig-leaf for his final exit, as demanded by Kabila.
A Mobutu aide, who asked not to be named, said it would be wrong to interpret the president's departure as a flight into exile. Mobutu, he recalled, had repeatedly ruled out fleeing.

Mobutu, 66 and battling prostate cancer, has seen his hold over Africa's third largest nation broken by a whirlwind rebel offensive. Many in Kinshasa, hungry for change, welcome the prospect of Kabila's arrival.
